item.description: Opportunity score: 80/100. Contract value: £25,000.00. Deadline: 2026-11-27 12:00 UTC. Positive indicators: training, value within target range, at least 7 days remaining. Risks/checks required: None. Original notice: https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/notice/90d317a4-0657-495a-a9ea-57e035554822. Advertised value: GBP 25,000 Status: active Deadline: 2026-11-27T12:00:00Z Official contract: https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/notice/90d317a4-0657-495a-a9ea-57e035554822 Backup search: https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Search?searchTerm=Activity%20%26%20Interpretation%20Plan%20Consultant View on OpenTenders Contract reference: ocds-b5fd17-daa551b3-034f-4997-98b2-a6dd293d4090 The appointed consultant will prepare a comprehensive Activity & Interpretation Plan which demonstrates how people will engage with St Peter's Church and the wider heritage of Thetford through: • Learning; • Volunteering; • Skills development; • Community engagement; • Interpretation; • Participation; • Events; • Training; • Outreach activities. The consultant shall ensure that the Activity & Interpretation Plan is fully aligned with NLHF requirements and capable of supporting a successful Delivery Phase application. The Activity Plan shall identify opportunities for community involvement, volunteering, learning, training, events and wider public engagement, together with recommendations for sustainable delivery and long-term legacy. The Interpretation Plan shall identify and communicate the key heritage themes, stories and significance of St Peter's Church, establish target audiences, and develop recommendations for accessible and engaging interpretation that supports the project's vision and outcomes. The Consultant shall ensure that both plans are fully integrated and aligned with the requirements of the National Lottery Heritage Fund and other funding stakeholders, providing a practical framework for implementation during the Delivery Phase. All Submissions should sent to Susan Moore - susanmoore@thetfordtowncouncil.gov.uk

Risks/checks required: None. Original notice: https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/notice/91ce9ffa-4f4e-4f2c-826c-070b55e93f87. Advertised value: GBP 10,000 Status: active Deadline: 2026-12-15T12:00:00Z Official contract: https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/notice/91ce9ffa-4f4e-4f2c-826c-070b55e93f87 Backup search: https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Search?searchTerm=CA18691%20-%20RFQ%202026/48%20-%20PEACEPLUS%20Roots%20Relationships%20Programme%20-%20Slieve%20Gullion%20DEA View on OpenTenders Contract reference: ocds-b5fd17-2c4ff32f-7c74-4afb-a215-0ddbb969af2d To deliver a community-led Arts, Crafts and Heritage Capacity Building Programme in the Slieve Gullion DEA, working with community groups from the Forkhill and Newtownhamilton areas. The programme should use arts, crafts, cultural heritage and creative skills development as a vehicle for building organisational capacity, increasing skills and confidence, supporting knowledge exchange, and creating opportunities for participants to learn from one another through practical activities, shared experiences and networking opportunities. The programme should celebrate and explore the rich cultural and heritage assets of the area while creating opportunities for participants from different backgrounds to connect, collaborate and develop lasting relationships. Through shared learning and creative engagement, participants will strengthen both their individual skills and the sustainability of their community organisations. This project will serve as both a community development initiative and a peacebuilding mechanism, creating sustained and meaningful contact across communities while strengthening local organisations and promoting appreciation of the area's diverse cultural heritage. To access this competition: Registered: Login to https://suppliers.multiquote.com and view the opportunity CA18691. Not registered: Visit https://suppliers.multiquote.com then register and quote CA18691 as the reason for registration. Any queries please contact MultiQuote on 020 3920 8054.
